raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60845.

With `--fully-sharded-loras`, the shared experts' LoRA layers all-gather / all-reduce across TP, and the routed experts' fused MoE LoRA kernel does its own collectives on the main stream. Running the shared experts on the aux stream puts two collectives in flight on the same communicator. Under CUDA graph capture they become independent graph branches, and the replay order is not guaranteed to match across ranks, so NCCL deadlocks (first LoRA decode step hangs, then `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`).

This PR runs the shared experts on the main stream when fully-sharded LoRA is enabled, same as the existing EPLB / flashinfer exclusions in `SharedExperts._disable_shared_experts_overlap`.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP=2, `--enable-lora --fully-sharded-loras --max-lora-rank 32`, default CUDA graphs, two rank-32 adapters alternating.

- v0.28.0 (reproduces the hang on the first LoRA request): with this patch, first request returns in 1s, 1000/1000 requests OK.
- v0.31.0 / main: 1000/1000 requests OK.

## Test Result

No hang, 0 failed in both runs.

This change only gates the CUDA shared-expert aux stream under fully-sharded LoRA, so those AMD pooling/init suites look unrelated — likely runner flakes. ## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

LGTM. The fix removes the concurrency instead of relying on enqueue order, and it matches the existing rule that LoRA's own dual stream is already disabled with `fully_sharded_loras` (`_build_lora_context`, `LoRAConfig` validation).

Validated on 2× H20 (TP=2, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 2D + 3D adapters, default CUDA graphs): v0.28.0 hangs on the first LoRA request (`RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`) and passes with `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1`. Current main does not hang on H20 (same as B200), so whether it triggers really depends on the hardware. This PR passes, and its outputs differ from main only by the usual run-to-run noise.

@@ -57,6 +58,15 @@ def __init__(
 
         self._mk_can_overlap_shared_experts = mk_can_overlap_shared_experts
 
+        # With fully-sharded LoRA the shared experts' LoRA layers issue TP
+        # collectives themselves, so they must not run on the aux stream
+        # (see _disable_shared_experts_overlap).
+        vllm_config = get_current_vllm_config_or_none()
+        lora_config = vllm_config.lora_config if vllm_config is not None else None
+        self._lora_fully_sharded = (
+            lora_config is not None and lora_config.fully_sharded_loras
+        )
+
         # Allow disabling of the separate shared experts stream for
         # debug purposes.
         # TODO: Remove this after more extensive testings with TP/DP
@@ -81,6 +91,15 @@ def _disable_shared_experts_overlap(self) -> bool:
         # Disable shared expert overlap if:
         #   - we are using eplb with non-safe backend, because of correctness issues
         #   - we are using flashinfer with DP, since there nothing to gain
+        #   - we are using fully-sharded LoRA: the shared experts' LoRA layers
+        #     all-gather / all-reduce across TP, and so does the routed
+        #     experts' fused MoE LoRA kernel on the main stream. Two
+        #     collectives in flight on the same communicator from different
+        #     streams become independent branches under CUDA graph capture,
+        #     and replay order is not guaranteed to match across ranks, which
+        #     deadlocks NCCL (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60845).
+        if self._lora_fully_sharded:
+            return True
